document_brief.narrative_theme: This succession plan aligns leadership continuity with business-critical risk by quantifying bench strength, naming high-potential successors, and closing emergency coverage gaps through time-bound development actions.

structure.heading: Bench Strength Assessment for Enterprise-Critical Roles (FY2026 Readiness Snapshot)
text_content: **Bench Strength Assessment for Enterprise-Critical Roles (FY2026 Readiness Snapshot)**

As of 01-05-2026 the enterprise succession review covers 12 critical leadership roles in scope. Current bench strength coverage is 75% (9 of 12 roles) with at least one “ready in 0–12 months” successor identified for each of those nine positions. This readiness determination reflects targeted assessment criteria including recent performance ratings, leadership potential evaluations, and validated readiness interviews conducted by People & Talent between January and April 2026. Where successors were classified as ready in 0–12 months, development plans emphasize stretch assignments, targeted coaching, and role-specific certification to ensure accelerated transition capability.

Despite the positive 75% bench coverage, three of the 12 critical roles lack a successor who is ready within 0–12 months, creating elevated exposure in specific enterprise functions. Emergency succession coverage is 58% (7 of 12 roles) with a named interim who can assume responsibilities within 14 days; conversely five roles currently have no designated interim. The risk assessment prioritizes the three uncovered roles and the five without immediate interim coverage for urgent succession planning, contingency staffing, and scenario-based exercises immediately.

The nine identified successors will be managed through individualized development tracks aligned to the enterprise Leadership Competency Framework and measurable performance milestones. Each track will document competency targets, a two-quarter progress review cadence, and specific sponsors (CHRO and function head) accountable for advancement. Development interventions include rotational assignments, executive coaching, and cross-functional immersion to close capability gaps before role transition. Progress will be tracked in the succession management system with quarterly reports to the CEO and Board beginning Q3 2026 onward.

2026. Action items include: 1. designate interim nominees and publish role responsibilities; 2. institute 14-day readiness drills for the seven roles that already have named interims; 3. implement cross-training plans for the three roles without 0–12 ready successors. Progress metrics will be reported monthly to the CEO and Enterprise Risk Committee stakeholders.

structure.heading: High-Potential Successor Slate, Development Plans, and Emergency Gap Remediation (Q3–Q4 2026)
text_content: **High-Potential Successor Slate, Development Plans, and Emergency Gap Remediation (Q3–Q4 2026)**

The FY2026 high-potential successor slate includes 8 candidates: Priya Nair, Miguel Santos, Aisha Khan, Daniel Cho, Elena Petrova, Marcus Reed, Sofia Alvarez, and Chen Wei. This slate was assembled from enterprise talent reviews conducted in Q1–Q2 2026 and reflects diversity across function, geography, and critical role readiness. Each candidate has an initial readiness rating and gap analysis; combined, the slate represents the primary pool for the next leadership tier. Succession metrics will be updated quarterly and reported to the executive council.

Individual development plans (IDPs) are tailored to close prioritized competency gaps identified for each successor candidate, with target KPIs tied to strategic outcomes such as cross-functional project delivery, P&L stewardship, and stakeholder influence. Development modalities include executive coaching, 9-month rotation opportunities, assessment center exercises, and targeted skills curricula. Quarterly calibration sessions will re-score readiness and update risk-adjusted promotion timelines; data will drive nomination for critical-role pilots and inform a 12-month forecast of readiness percentages for enterprise-critical positions and leadership bench.

There are 5 emergency succession gaps where no interim is identified today; this represents an immediate enterprise risk requiring prioritized remediation. Each gap will have a named interim and a 30-60-90 day transition checklist completed by 15-08-2026, with completion certifiable by the HR Risk Office. Remediation actions include rapid interim nomination, formal handover playbooks, mandatory shadowing, and a contingency communication plan. Risk owners in the impacted business units and the Chief Human Resources Officer will confirm readiness and execute tabletop exercises.
